title: University of Surrey Study: Digital Inclusion Funding 'Misses the Mark' Despite Two Decades of Investment
detail: A peer-reviewed study from the University of Surrey, published in Management and Organization Review and widely reported on May 9, 2026, found that millions across Asia, Africa, Latin America, and Oceania remain excluded from meaningful digital participation despite sustained international investment. Drawing on evidence from 122 studies across the Global South, the core finding was that the biggest barrier to impact is fragmentation — governments, private sector actors, and international organizations consistently act in parallel but rarely in genuine partnership. The study called for coordinated multi-stakeholder digital inclusion frameworks with binding accountability mechanisms, rather than isolated single-pillar programs that fail the most marginalized communities.

title: US: National Digital Inclusion Alliance Launches DEA Month of Action Marking One Year Since Digital Equity Act Cancellation
detail: The National Digital Inclusion Alliance (NDIA) launched its 'DEA Month of Action' on May 8 (running through June 8, 2026), marking the one-year anniversary of President Trump's cancellation of the $2.75 billion Digital Equity Act via social media post. The campaign aims to raise awareness of the program's cancellation, lobby Congress to restore digital equity funding in the FY2027 budget, and highlight impacts on libraries, community organizations, and low-income households that had relied on state Digital Equity Act allocations. A virtual press conference with Members of Congress and civil society leaders followed the May 8 launch. The Digital Equity Act had been designed to fund state digital inclusion plans, affordability programs, and digital literacy training for millions of underconnected Americans.
